entries.title: Where it sits starts searching when opened
entries.body: Choosing Where it sits in Sources, on one of your own articles, starts its search of the published research if none has been run, with no second click. Results open on an overview with its own chat button, and counts that jump to each group of findings, Challenged first. Following a link, reloading or going Back never starts a search, and a finished search is not re-run on its own. The privacy page says when this happens.

entries.title: Research findings appear beside the passages they concern
entries.body: What Where it sits found about a passage, such as Challenged, Supported or Since, appears as a note in the margin beside that passage, without the Experimental features switch. You see these notes on your own articles once the search has been run; people reading an article you share do not.

entries.title: Narrow a much-cited piece's citations by topic
entries.body: For a much-cited piece, After it in Where it sits has a switch between Most cited and About "its main topic", which lists only the citing works on that topic. That list is fetched only when you ask for it. The switch could wait forever after you moved between articles; that is fixed.

entries.title: Possible citations when none can be listed
entries.body: Where Sources would say it cannot list who cites an article, it can show Possible citations: works found by searching for the article's title, counted, with a link to the same search at OpenAlex. They are unchecked matches, from papers only. It applies only to some articles added from a web address, and needs Experimental features on your profile.

entries.title: Two ways to judge findings before the verdict
entries.body: With Experimental features on, Where it sits has an Experiments row. Guess first shows the passages it found with their labels hidden until you press Reveal; Evidence first sets a passage beside a source's quote and asks whether the source supports, challenges or updates it, then reveals. Neither starts a search or saves your choices.

entries.title: The add box no longer carries small print
entries.body: The note that an added article's text is sent to outside services for processing has moved from under the add box in your library into the information button beside File, which also appears in Upload a file instead. The page you see while an article is being added still shows it.

entries.title: Home-screen and email icons have a dark background
entries.body: Adding Spideryarn to an Apple home screen gives an icon with a charcoal background, or a cream one if your phone is set to light mode. The Android install icons and the logo in our emails are charcoal too. An icon already on your home screen does not change; add it again to get the new one.

entries.title: Findings opened from the margin keep their place
entries.body: Opening a research finding from a note in the margin, or from a chat about it, lost track of which finding you wanted if Where it sits failed to load its saved results. After a successful retry, it opens the finding's group and scrolls to it.
